definition: A phrasal template is a phrase-long collocation that contains one or several empty slots which may be filled by words to produce individual phrases..
details: A phrasal template is a phrase-long collocation that contains one or several empty slots which may be filled by words to produce individual phrases.

explainer.lead: A phrasal template is a fixed phrase containing blank slots to be filled with words. It matters for generating many variants of a phrase from one structure.

tiers.eli5: It is a sentence with gaps, like mad-libs, where you drop in different words to make new phrases.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use templates to mass-produce structured text or test utterances. Pitfall: templates fixed in advance produce repetitive output that misses unanticipated phrasing.
tiers.paperLevel: A phrase-long collocation containing one or several empty slots filled by words to produce individual phrases; its generality is bounded by the fixed surrounding text.

explainer.example: “The ___ sat on the ___” filled with “cat” and “mat” yields “The cat sat on the mat.”
